Concrete Driveways · Anna Maria Island, FL

Concrete Driveways Across Anna Maria Island's Three Cities

A concrete driveway on Anna Maria Island runs $6–$15 per sq ft installed as of October 2026. Anna Maria, Holmes Beach and Bradenton Beach each review a driveway permit through their own department, and Holmes Beach's code sets specific width and setback numbers the other two cities don't publish the same way.

By the Opera Concrete & Pavers estimating team · Updated October 1, 2026

Holmes Beach's own numbers for a narrow island lot

Holmes Beach caps the combined width of a driveway on a lot under 75 feet wide at half the lot's own width, measured where the drive meets the right-of-way, and keeps any driveway at least 10 feet from a street-line intersection or 6 feet along the right-of-way line, 6 feet from a side property line and 10 feet from the next driveway over Holmes Beach Code, zoning supplemental standards. Those numbers matter on an island where plenty of lots are narrower than a mainland subdivision lot to begin with.

When a Sandy Lot Still Has Clay Pockets

Not every sandy Florida lot is sand all the way down. Soils like Pomona and Felda look like typical fine sand at the surface, but a few feet down they change into a sandy clay loam or sandy clay layer that drains and compacts differently than the material above it. Grading a Anna Maria Island driveway base, we expect that kind of shift rather than treating the whole excavation as one uniform material, because a compactor set up for loose sand will not do the same job on a denser clay pocket. Missing that change is one of the quieter reasons a base looks fine at pour time and still settles unevenly a year later.

Anna Maria and Bradenton Beach confirm case by case

Anna Maria's own code addresses driveway pavers placed in the right-of-way directly, under a permit the Building Department issues with Public Works sign-off, but a straightforward on-lot driveway question there, like one in Bradenton Beach, gets confirmed with that city's own department rather than assumed from a neighboring city's rule City of Anna Maria, Building Department City of Bradenton Beach, Building & Planning. Since Bradenton Beach sits entirely within a FEMA flood zone, a driveway tied into a storm rebuild there often comes with an elevation certificate already on file, which the permit review references directly.

Why a 4-Inch Slab Isn't Enough for a Boat Trailer

A standard 4-inch driveway is built for cars and light trucks, not for an RV, a boat trailer or anything that concentrates weight on a narrow set of wheels. For that kind of load, we take the slab to 5 or 6 inches thick, which spreads the weight over more concrete and resists the point-load cracking a thinner slab would show first. Anyone in Anna Maria Island planning to park something heavier than a daily driver should say so before the forms go in, since thickening a finished driveway later means tearing it out. Mix strength matters too, but added thickness does more for a point load than extra psi alone.

Rebuilding a driveway after storm damage on a narrow Holmes Beach lot, worked out in square feet

Picture a 60-foot-wide Holmes Beach lot with an 18 by 40 foot driveway, 720 square feet, that cracked and settled after 2024's storm surge undermined the base beneath it. At $6–$15 per sq ft installed, the new pour runs $4,320 to $10,800, tightening to roughly $5,760 to $8,640 inside the typical $8–$12 band. Because the lot is under 75 feet wide, the new driveway's width still has to clear half the lot's own width at the right-of-way line, the same limit that applied before the storm.

Why the Saw Comes Out Hours, Not Days, After the Pour

Joint cutting happens on a tight clock relative to the pour, not on a separate visit days later. Depending on the saw and the weather, cuts go in anywhere from about 1 hour to about 12 hours after finishing, timed to when the concrete has firmed up enough to cut cleanly without the edge crumbling. On a Anna Maria Island job, we track the slab's set time rather than work from a fixed schedule, since a hot, dry afternoon firms concrete up faster than an overcast one. Missing that window in either direction is how a joint ends up ragged or badly placed relative to where the slab actually wants to crack.

A Driveway Can Lift Years After the Tree Was Already There

Live oak roots keep growing long after a driveway is poured, and a root that was not a problem at install can lift a slab edge five or ten years later. Orlando, Winter Park and Sarasota all protect larger trees by ordinance, and cutting into a protected root system without a permit can be a code violation even if the tree itself looks like it is just dropping leaves on the driveway. A Anna Maria Island homeowner who notices a slab edge starting to tent near a mature tree is better off checking the local tree ordinance before calling anyone with a saw, since the fix has to account for the tree's status, not just the concrete.

Watching for Root Heave Before It Becomes a Crack

A slab edge that starts to tent or lift slightly near a mature oak is an early sign of root growth underneath, worth noticing before it turns into a full crack. Orlando and Winter Park both regulate trees at 6 inches in diameter by ordinance, so the right first move in a Anna Maria Island yard with a protected tree nearby is checking the local rule, not reaching for a shovel or a saw. Catching heave early sometimes lets a contractor address the slab section without disturbing the root system at all, where waiting until the crack is severe narrows the options considerably.

Frequently asked questions

Which city issues my driveway permit on Anna Maria Island?

Whichever of the three incorporated cities the address sits in: Anna Maria, Holmes Beach or Bradenton Beach. Each runs a separate building department, so the permit never goes to a county office or to one of the other two cities.

Does Holmes Beach limit how wide a driveway can be?

On a lot under 75 feet wide, yes. The combined driveway width at the right-of-way line is capped at half the lot's own width, on top of separate setback distances from intersections, property lines and neighboring driveways.

Does a driveway rebuild in Bradenton Beach need flood paperwork?

Often, yes, since the city sits entirely within a FEMA-mapped flood zone. A rebuild tied to storm damage commonly references an elevation certificate or a substantial-damage determination already on file with the city.
